findings.title: Second downsize definition overrides the width/height version
findings.body: Ruby replaces a method when it is defined again, so the three-argument downsize defined here makes the width/height downsize at line 145 dead code. Any existing caller passing from, to, width, and height will now raise ArgumentError instead of resizing, breaking the previous public API. The two signatures need to be merged or given different names.

findings.title: Percentage downsizing does not work correctly for animated GIFs
findings.body: This passes the dimension string "80%" while forwarding SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. For an animated GIF, OptimizedImage dispatches to the gifsicle path, whose --resize-fit option expects pixel geometry such as 800x600 rather than a percentage, so the command can fail or produce an unintended size. When animated thumbnails are disabled, the ordinary ImageMagick path reads only frame [0], silently flattening an uploaded animated GIF based on a thumbnail preference rather than preserving the original animation.

findings.title: Failed in-place downsizing can corrupt the uploaded file
findings.body: The same tempfile path is used as both conversion source and destination, and the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored. If conversion or ImageOptim fails, the loop retries up to five times against a file that may have been partially overwritten and then line 72 uploads whatever bytes remain, instead of retaining the original file or returning a clean error. Conversion should write to a separate temporary file and replace the upload only after success.

findings.title: Remote-download limit ignores the configured maximum size
findings.body: API URL downloads are now always capped at a hard-coded 10 megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Sites that configured a lower limit will have the server fetch, store temporarily, and process files beyond their policy, while sites that configured a higher limit are incorrectly capped; the new image-only downsizer also does not make oversized non-image downloads conform to the relevant attachment limit.

findings.title: Client validation hard-codes 10 MB for every upload type
findings.body: validateUploadedFile receives a type but no longer uses Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so image and attachment limits are both replaced by 10 MB. Administrators with smaller limits get avoidable large uploads and server-side rejections, administrators with larger limits get incorrect client-side rejections, and the 413 handler at line 246 similarly reports 10 MB regardless of the configured limit.
